summary: Nine of the AKC's top 10 are household names and a casual player finds 8, with the German Shorthaired Pointer as the fair stretch. Famous misses (Husky, Chihuahua, Pug, Corgi) burn lives fast, and most show no rank.
reasons: Casual found French Bulldog, Lab, Golden, German Shepherd, Poodle, Beagle, Bulldog and Dachshund, then lost 4 lives on Husky, Chihuahua, Corgi and Pug. Only Corgi shows a rank (#10 in 2019). A player who starts with small dogs (Chihuahua, Pug, Yorkie, Shih Tzu) can be out with 4.

The title names the measure, and the usual US wrong answers are handled: pit bull, labradoodle and goldendoodle are free, and frenchie, golden, lab, doxie, wiener dog, rottie, gsp and english bulldog all match. The fan gets 10/10 without a miss.
Wikipedia has no AKC ranks past 10, so most misses can't show a figure. The page's other numbers (FCI 2013, UK 2015) would mislead on a US list, so this is a limit of the source, not a fix.
fixes: Crossbreeds typed with a space or hyphen are offered as a parent breed: "golden doodle", "golden doodles", "golden-doodle" and "golden mountain doodle" offer #3 Golden Retriever; "aussie doodle" offers Australian Shepherd, "bernese doodle" Bernese Mountain Dog, "yorkie poo" Yorkshire Terrier (each a life if confirmed). Match the knownOnly crossbreed names with spaces and hyphens removed (or add those spellings) so they stay free.

"pointer" alone is offered as #9 German Shorthaired Pointer, though the topic's junkAliases comment says the game should ask which, and the AKC's breed named Pointer is in the pool as English Pointer. Make it offer the choice (German Shorthaired Pointer, English Pointer, German Wirehaired Pointer) the way "retriever" does. "shepherd" alone goes straight to #4 German Shepherd the same way.
Add "French Poodle" and "French Poodles" as aliases of #6 Poodle: "french poodle" is a common US name for it and currently gets "not an answer for this list".
